title: Procurement vs Purchasing: What's the Difference?
snippet: In P2P, procurement typically produces the things that make execution predictable: Supplier standards: approved vendors, onboarding requirements, risk/compliance checks · Commercial terms: pricing, discounts, SLAs, payment terms, renewals, contract language · Buying rules: preferred suppliers, spend thresholds, approval paths, category guardrails · Sourcing decisions: when to single-source vs multi-source, how quotes are evaluated Structuring intake so requests include the details procurement needs (category, vendor, justification, budget owner, timing) Applying guardrails early through purchase approval paths, spend thresholds, and preferred supplier rules · Operationalizing sourcing for higher-risk or higher-value purchases (quotes, evaluations, and exception justification) One reason procurement looks beyond sticker price is total cost of ownership (TCO)—the full cost of an item over its useful life. TCO can include shipping, implementation, training, maintenance, renewals, and the operational cost of delays, errors, or exceptions. Example (off-contract buy): Marketing needs branded swag fast and picks a random vendor. Procurement has a preferred supplier with negotiated pricing and net-30 terms, but the request bypasses intake. Purchasing receives an invoice with a credit-card fee and net-7 terms — and no PO.

A family business built on Italian creativity and international innovation, at the forefront of the industry’s offerings of raw materials, ambitiously gaining control of mines for raw materials such as zirconium with Industrie Bitossi and boric acid with Inkabor, and manufacturing a complete range of elements for the industry, including frits (with a total production of over 400.000 tons per year), glazes, pigments, digital inks, enamel glazes, grinding media, lead oxide, and glass products, as well as providing operating logistics. ↳ Read less ## A Global Family 29 companies in 18 countries, including Spain, Poland, Mexico, Brazil, Indonesia, India, Vietnam, Portugal, China, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, and a new service facility in the United States. ↳ Read more It counts among its affiliate companies Industrie Bitossi, Inkabor, Minerals 2000, Mariter, Eurit, Colorobbia Art, Bitossi Ceramiche, Bitossi Home, and the Ce.Ri.Col research laboratory. ↳ Read less ![](https://gruppocolorobbia.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/ColorobbiaFiorano_601PAZ_6244_Lres.jpg)![](https://gruppocolorobbia.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/ColorobbiaFiorano_275PAN_0185_Lres-1.jpg) ## Over 2000 employees Over 600 milions euro turnover Today, the Colorobbia Group is responsible for 13% on the international ceramics industry. ![](https://dev.andreamantegazza.it/colorobbia/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/PUTTI.jpg) ## Italian creativity Founded by Guido Bitossi in 1921, the now legendary Bitossi brand began as a refined craft producer of the area’s eminent Renaissance tableware traditions. In the post-war boom he spearheaded Italy’s first modern iterations of ceramics with prominent designer collaborations. Led by the company’s celebrated artistic director Aldo Londi, Bitossi revolutionized the ceramic world with designs by Ettore Sottsass and others. It was this contemporary spirit that would propel the Bitossi family to enlarge, under the name of the Colorobbia Group, as the first major supplier for the ceramic industry to go global. ↳ Read more The post-war period ushered in expansion as well, when Bitossi founded the Colorificio Ceramico Della Robbia in honor of the Renaissance master ceramics sculptor, Andrea della Robbia, whose virtuoso putti for the Ospedale degli Innocenti would inspire the Colorobbia logo. From its Italian foundations, the Colorobbia Group continues to grow internationally through design and research, with the Bitossi leadership extending the company’s family-forged bonds to its over 2000 employees and its worldwide clients in 75 countries. ↳ Read less Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication • Sustainability • Ethics • Worldwide Services • Italian Creativity • Dedication ## Research and Innovation The company has established itself as the vanguard of digital printing for tiles and tableware by continually devising new techniques, better performing inks, and greater decorative possibilities, while expanding its capacities with innovations in textiles and glass derived from its ceramic expertise. 5% of the turnover is invested in R&D. ↳ Read more The Colorobbia Group has unveiled high-quality water-based pigmented textile inks for that offer a fast, flexible, and ecofriendly innovation. And broadening its horizons, the group has launched groundbreaking methods for the decoration and coloration of glass. The company is also the first to open the door to new digital decoration techniques bringing precious metal embellishments to tableware, tiles, and glass — a water-based digital glazed of a technique previously limited to manual application until the Colorobbia Group’s innovative headway. The introduction of patented PHOEBE system, will constitute a revolution in the possibilities of contemporary ceramic production, amplifying present-day production beyond the previous leap forward of digital ink ceramic printing. ↳ Read less ![](https://gruppocolorobbia.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/ColorobbiaFiorano_342PAZ_6127_Lres.jpg)![](https://gruppocolorobbia.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/ColorobbiaFiorano_527PAZ_5866_Lres.jpg) ![](https://gruppocolorobbia.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/ColorobbiaFiorano_355PAZ_6140ed-scaled.jpg)![](https://gruppocolorobbia.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Natura5-scaled.jpg) ## Sustainability and Ethics Since its founding, the Colorobbia Group has always maintained a philosophy that respects environmental sustainability, with protocols that rigorously align with the guidelines of every country in which it is present. The sensibility informs an approach of extreme efficiency in all stages of production, ensuring that energy and materials are conserved to the utmost degree, plus recycling and treating industrial-use water, reusing raw materials, and reducing atmospheric emissions. ↳ Read more The ethic extends to the entire Colorobbia workforce. Acute attention to safeguarding working condition means that all products and activities are scrutinized for the upmost of safety, in manufacturing facilities and across the entire span of company sites, with protection devices, ventilation, and the transport of raw materials carefully analyzed for the maximum of security, and all suppliers are equally examined to maintain high standards. ↳ Read less ## Fondazione Vittoriano Bitossi Honoring its profound bond with the territory, in 2008 the family launched the Vittoriano Bitossi Foundation for ceramics inside the original Montelupo Fiorentino factory where the business was born in 1921. ↳ Read more The foundation welcomes visitors to explore the archive of the company’s tools, documents, and ceramics dating from its entire history. Actualidad Castellón 26 de octubre de 2023 4 min. La Diputación Provincial y la Cámara de Comercio de Castellón impulsan una nueva edición del WorkForum Castellón, un evento que pretende ser un espacio en el que se promueve el empleo de calidad ofreciendo las mejores oportunidades profesionales, así como satisfacer las necesidades de contratación de las empresas de nuestra provincia. La presidenta de la Diputación Provincial de Castellón, Marta Barrachina, y la presidenta de la Cámara de Comercio de Castellón, María Dolores Guillamón, se han reunido para ultimar los detalles de la novena edición que tendrá lugar el próximo jueves 15 de noviembre en la Cámara de Comercio de Castellón de 9.00 a 18.00 horas. La primera presidenta de la Diputación ha indicado que “las sinergias entre la Diputación de Castellón y la Cámara de Comercio son de gran importancia al permitir estimular la economía en la provincia y, por tanto abrir nuevas oportunidades laborales, que se traducen en oportunidades de crecimiento y bienestar en nuestro territorio”. Esas nuevas oportunidades se materializarán, un año más, en el WorkForum Castellón que se va a convertir en un punto de encuentro entre responsables de Recursos Humanos de empresas y personas candidatas, todos ellos en búsqueda de nuevas oportunidades, así como de asistentes interesados en aprender más sobre los retos del mercado de trabajo. Este evento está dirigido a todas las personas de la provincia de Castellón que se encuentren en búsqueda activa de empleo o de mejora de su situación laboral. Las personas que participen en el foro podrán inscribirse en las ofertas de empleo y, en caso de cumplir los requisitos, participar en procesos de selección con los responsables de Recursos Humanos de diferentes empresas durante toda la jornada. Las inscripciones a las ofertas de empleo estarán abiertas a partir de este viernes 27 de octubre y se puede acceder desde la web del evento www.workforumcastellon.es hasta el día 10 de noviembre. La presidenta de la Cámara de Comercio de Castellón tiene la confianza de que “un año más este foro facilitará el acceso laboral a personas en situación de desempleo o la mejora profesional de quienes aspiran a ello, gracias a la participación de las empresas y la diversidad de puestos de trabajo ofertados, y cómo no, a la colaboración entre las instituciones como lo venimos haciendo desde hace años la Diputación y la Cámara de Comercio de Castellón” A día de hoy, las empresas que han confirmado su participación
